metadata.notes: Chapter spans about twenty days after the opening negotiation scene.

believes: There may be additional survivor groups elsewhere in Sol beyond Colonel Butterworth's refugees.
Titan and the Oort station might possibly still contain humans until the survey reports come back.
learns: Titan and the Oort station have both been abandoned and contain no responding humans.
Recovered battle wreckage in Sol provides enough refined material to begin industrial buildup for colony ship construction.

characters_present.name: Colonel George Butterworth
characters_present.notes: Appears via communications during negotiations over evacuation priorities.

characters_present.name: Homer
characters_present.notes: Assisting with surveys and resource recovery in Sol.

planets.name: Titan
planets.notes: Survey drones report the station at Titan abandoned and not attacked.

communications.contents_summary: Riker and Butterworth argue again over whether searching for other survivor groups should compete with colony-ship preparation.
communications.notes: Conversation is effectively local-system communication during ongoing negotiations.

infrastructure.notes: Small autofactories are set up at recovered material sites to process wreckage and produce cargo drones.
Larger autofactories are established at the Earth/Moon L4 and L5 points to produce new Bobs, drones, and later industrial equipment for colony ships.
Initial buildup begins at Earth/Moon L4 and L5 toward a shipyard capable of constructing full-sized colony ships.

relationships.text: Riker and Butterworth continue to clash over priorities, with Butterworth pressing refugee welfare and Riker insisting on the project's critical path.
Homer reassures Riker of his commitment to helping surviving humans and supports the evacuation effort professionally.

scenes.summary: Riker argues with Colonel Butterworth about whether to spend effort searching for other survivor groups while preparing colony ships.
Homer reports promising salvage finds and ongoing surveys of remote stations, and Riker reviews the daunting project plan.
Homer completes the survey, confirms Titan and the Oort station are abandoned, and begins establishing salvage autofactories and industrial buildup at Earth/Moon L4 and L5.

quotes.speaker: Homer
quotes.text: Each of us is different, Riker, but not different enough to not care.
quotes.context: Homer explains why he is taking the human rescue effort seriously despite his usual joking demeanor.

events.text: Riker and Homer secure enough salvage in Sol to begin building the industrial base for humanity's evacuation, establishing autofactories at recovery sites and larger production hubs at Earth/Moon L4 and L5.

summary.one_line: Riker and Homer move the Sol evacuation plan from negotiation into industrial buildup after confirming enough salvage exists to start construction.
summary.paragraph: Riker's negotiations with Colonel Butterworth remain tense, especially over whether to divert effort into searching for other survivor enclaves, but Riker holds firm on following the project's critical path. Homer reports several promising salvage sites from old space battles and continues surveying remote stations for resources or survivors. Twenty days later, the surveys confirm that Titan and the Oort station are abandoned, but the recovered wreckage is sufficient to begin bootstrapping production. Small autofactories are established at salvage sites, while larger facilities at Earth/Moon L4 and L5 begin scaling toward Bob production, drone manufacture, and eventually colony-ship construction. Riker reflects on how deeply he has been pulled back into responsibility for humanity's survival.
events: Riker and Colonel Butterworth argue again about whether searching for other survivor groups should take priority during evacuation planning.
Homer reports promising salvage finds from old battles and says drones are nearing Titan and the Oort station.
Homer tells Riker that, despite their differences, any Bob should care about humans who may die without help.
Twenty days later, the surveys confirm that Titan and the Oort station were abandoned rather than attacked.
Homer begins setting up small autofactories at salvage sites to process recovered material and ship it inward.
Larger autofactories are established at Earth/Moon L4 and L5 to bootstrap production toward full colony-ship construction.
Riker reflects on the scale of responsibility now resting on him as humanity's evacuation becomes a real industrial project.
summary.pov_emotional_arc: Riker moves from frustration and fatigue over political wrangling to sober determination as the evacuation effort finally gains practical momentum.

known_planets: Alpha Centauri B inner asteroid belt

open_threads.text: Bob now knows replicants can go insane during unstructured subjective time, raising the question of whether he can stay sane through training and standby.
Bob is denied access to genealogy records and remains cut off from any living descendants or family connections.
Bob learns that hostile factions inside FAITH could sabotage or terminate the replicant project.
Bob now knows several rival nations are racing to launch interstellar probes, with the Brazilian Empire suspected of sabotage and armed competition.
Bob learns the FAITH facility has a hidden tactical nuclear failsafe that could kill him and everyone nearby if someone decides he is too dangerous.
Minister Jacoby leaves after threatening Dr. Landers, raising the question of whether he will act against the replicant project.
The launch turns into a confused orbital battle with missiles, military ships, and multiple unknown attackers, leaving the identity of the factions involved unresolved.
Bob detects apparent nuclear detonations on Earth after hearing of escalating conflict, leaving the scale of the war and Sol's survival uncertain.
After disabling his endocrine control system, Bob begins fully mourning his lost human life, raising the question of how this emotional release will affect him going forward.
Bob concludes that at least one more Brazilian Empire ship exists and that USE, Chinese, and possibly Australian probes may also be active somewhere in space.
Bob's first cohort of clones diverges in personality immediately, raising questions about how future Bob society and identity will evolve.
Milo has found two apparently habitable living worlds at Omicron Eridani, but it remains unresolved whether Earth life and humans are biologically compatible with them.
Milo departs for 82 Eridani, opening the question of what he will find there.
Bill and Garfield now have a working subspace communications system, raising the question of how quickly they can deploy it across multiple star systems.
Riker and Colonel Butterworth agree to try building colony ships in Sol, raising the question of whether the surviving humans can endure long enough to launch them and where they will go.
Bob has discovered intelligent fire-using natives on Delta Eridani 4, raising the question of whether and how he will make first contact.
One Brazilian vessel escapes the destruction of the Alpha Centauri construction yard, leaving its destination and future threat unresolved.
Calvin and Goku conclude Alpha Centauri should be reinforced with combat-class Bobs, raising the question of whether Bill will approve and send them.

recent_events.text: Bill and Garfield achieve a breakthrough by successfully testing real-time subspace communication.
Riker's mysterious hail turns out to be surviving USE forces, who ask for Bob help to build colony ships and evacuate humanity from dying Earth.
Bob reaches Delta Eridani, starts building up the system, and discovers intelligent alien life on its promising habitable world.
Calvin finds the lost USE probe's wreckage in Alpha Centauri B, then joins Goku in destroying a Brazilian construction yard in Alpha Centauri A.
Riker and Homer move the Sol evacuation plan from negotiation into industrial buildup after confirming enough salvage exists to start construction.
